newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee shade firmer after dollar softens.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee shade firmer after dollar softens.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee was quoted slightly higher due to overseas softening of the dollar against most major currencies, dealers said on Wednesday.
The rupee was quoted at 57.12 to the dollar but remained untraded at 0345 GMT nearly two hours after the market opened, they said. It closed at 57.16 to the dollar on Tuesday.
"The dollar opened low since dealers had factored in the overseas easing," said an ANZ Gridlays Bank dealer.
He said the Central Bank action of pushing down the dollar by half a local cent, also showed the authorities were comefortable with the current dollar-rupee exchange rate.
The Central Bank fixed buying and selling prices at 56.0241 and 57.1559.
"The Central Bank could have really pushed down the dollar more if they were uncomfortable," said an American Express Bank dealer.
The exchange rate is expected to remain tight between 57.12 and 57.16, supported by import covering, dealers said.
Overnight call money was at 16 percent after closing at 15, due to two big state banks borrowing in the market, dealers said.
